So if i am new and want to start nootropics for school use, for cheap, which ones should i take for my stack and what suppliers?

The best nootropics ever are (I warn you this may be a little disappointing):

  1. Good sleep
  2. Good food
  3. Sports and fitness

If you think your nutrition is optimal, you eat your macro and micronutrients, get enough vitamins, fiber, etc. and you sleep at least 8 hours every night, and do some physical activity at least three times a week, then you can start experimenting with different stuff. The thing is, what works for me or somebody else on the internet, won't necessary work for you too. Nootropics and cognitive enhancement is a relatively new field of study and unfortunately you will have to do your own research. The basic, popular stuff is caffeine and l-theanine, piracetam, creatin, and various plant based supplements, like gingko biloba and ginseng, but I cannot stress enough the importance of the three things I mentioned in my first sentence. Sleep well, eat good brain food, exercise, and then add the chemicals.

If you are new, google is your friend, and be safe my friend ;) Of course you should consult your doctor, before taking any supplements or drugs.

mrlkts has the right idea. Since going to the gym a couple of times a week, eating 1 or less fast food meals per week, doing a small exercise routine each morning, situps etc. and getting good sleep each night (9 hours for me) I've 100% increased my concentration, ability to recall information, confidence and mood.

Getting other stuff might help you, might not.

  • l-theanine / caffeine combo is a good starter. Get all the benefits of caffeine with far fewer downsides.

I take a 100mg caffeine with 250mg l-theanine every morning. Again in the afternoon if you need to get a lot done.

I bought both of these off amazon pretty cheap. Got 50g l-theanine (about 200 serves) for $15 and 100 100mg caffeine pills for less than $10. Might look at taking 200mg caffeine pills instead once my caffeine tolerance goes up. I bought the l-theanine from bulksupplements and it arrived pretty quick, seems to be good but you can try other dealers.

  • Creatine doesn't seem to help memory but definitely gives me an energy boost.

I take 5grams in the morning and another 5 grams in the afternoon if I'm going to the gym. I got a kilo (200 serves) for like $10 off amazon.

  • Bacopa monnieri can help memory recollection and turning short term memory into long term memory.

I've just started taking 250mg extract pills which I got off amazon for $10 (90 pills). I don't think I've noticed anything yet but studies have proven its usefulness.

  • Ritalin and Modafinil

I have tried both in the past and would say that both of these could help you study. Ritalin did nothing for me but might help you concentrate if you have attention problems. Modafinil 100% worked for me. It gave me a great mood boost, made me feel really sociable and helped me recall information which I'd barely paid attention to in class really easily. It also helped me to really focus on one thing. However, its not great for essay writing and can make some people pretty anxious. A friend on modafinil struggled trying to concentrate on all the interconnecting parts of an essay and it really made her anxious.

  • Choline bitartate works great in combo with piracetam but I haven't tried it personally.

I take 5 grams a day. I got a kilo (200 serves) for about $25 on amazon.

TL;DR caffeine/l-theanine combo, piracetam/choline bitartate combo, creatine, modafinil, bacopa monnieri, sleep, exercise and good food is probably one of the best stacks you can make.
